Subject: VPC endpoint & auth/routing scope — post-demo next steps

Hi Maria / Ivan —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared scope for the private connectivity and SDK/auth work: 

Recap (what we covered)
- Hosted vs Private: you want a private deployment (VPC endpoint) for production inference and hosted for dev/testing.
- Auth: token-based SDK auth for app traffic + option for mTLS between your VPC and Redwood egress gateway for extra assurance.
- Routing & egress: prefer customer egress through a VPC endpoint (no NAT) + outbound DNS allowlist to our resolver for model fetches.
- Structured output & tool-calling: we covered using the SDK with structured JSON responses and a lightweight reranker on embeddings for search results.

Open questions / items we need from FinStack
1) IP allowlist: can you share the CIDR ranges for the VPC endpoint and any egress NAT IPs (we provided an example template attached)?
2) KMS/HSM: confirm whether you want Redwood to use your KMS or our managed keys for model logs and audit records.
3) Embeddings workload: expected QPS and average request size (tokens) so we can recommend instance sizing and quantization profile.
4) mTLS: do you have a cert-authority / internal PKI or should we coordinate a short-lived cert exchange?

Proposed next steps
- Maria/Ivan: send IP allowlist CSV + preferred KMS approach (by EOD Friday).
- Internal: Ben to draft a minimal network diagram + endpoint config we’ll hand to your infra team.
- Internal: Lauren to prepare an SDK quickstart snippet showing token auth + structured output example (tool-calling stub).

Attached: redwood_private_connectivity_summary.pdf (overview) and ip-allowlist-template.csv

If that timeline works I’ll book a 30m follow-up with your infra lead for next week.

Thanks,
Priyom Das

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our infra side: 

- IP ranges: attaching our current egress ranges — we've labeled them in the CSV. Note we run a pair of NAT gateways in us-west-2 and an internal peering fleet; the CIDRs are included.
- KMS: we prefer to use our AWS KMS CMKs for any customer-specific logs/encryption; we can provide IAM role bindings.
- mTLS: we have an internal PKI and can issue a server certificate for Redwood if needed; please advise the required SANs.
- Embeddings: initial throughput is modest — ~10 qps peak for embedding creation and ~30 qps for reranking/search queries; typical payloads are 512 tokens.

Two requests: can you confirm whether the VPC endpoint will require a route-table change (for private DNS) or simply an ENI-based endpoint in our subnet? Also, what latency SLOs do you see for embedding/rerank at that QPS?

Ivan, CC’ing you to follow on the networking side.

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: VPC endpoint & auth/routing scope — post-demo next steps

Maria / Ivan — quick technical reply to the network questions + latency SLOs.

Thanks for sending the ranges. Short answers: 
- Endpoint type: we recommend an interface VPC endpoint (ENI-backed) in your private subnets. That avoids changing route tables and preserves your existing NAT behavior. If you prefer gateway endpoints we can discuss, but for our control-plane traffic an interface endpoint is simpler.
- Private DNS: we will register a private DNS name for the endpoint and provide the CNAME you need for split-horizon if desired. No route-table edits required for interface endpoints.
- IP allowlist: we will provide the egress IPs you should allow; these are the IPs our endpoint ENIs will use and the control-plane callouts. Expect a small set (typically 4–8 IPv4 addresses) per region.
- mTLS: since you have an internal PKI, we can support mTLS using your CA. We’ll need the expected SANs and whether the certs are rotated via an API or manually.
- KMS: we support customer-managed CMKs via cross-account IAM roles; we will share the minimal policy.

Latency SLOs for embeddings/rerank at the volumes you quoted (~10–30 QPS):
- Embedding generation (512 tokens): p50 ~ 70ms, p95 ~ 210ms on our recommended quantized instance family;
- Rerank (dense vector scores + small model): p50 ~ 40ms, p95 ~ 150ms.

Action items (internal owners):
- Ben: create a one-page network diagram + list of ENI IPs (ETA 24h).
- Lauren: SDK code snippet showing token auth, example for structured output/function calling, and small reranker sample (ETA 48h).
- Marissa: coordinate a short canary plan for private endpoints on Dedicated capacity if FinStack needs a separate SLAs flow (ETA 48h).

If helpful, we can also schedule a 30-minute deep-dive with your infra team to walk the endpoint provisioning steps.

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
